question: In 2022, Former Supreme Court Justice ___________ was appointed chairperson of the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (NDIAC).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hemant Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Hemant Gupta, a former Supreme Court judge, was appointed Chairperson of the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre (NDIAC) in December 2022, about two months after his retirement from the Supreme Court. (न्यायमूर्ति हेमंत गुप्ता — नई दिल्ली अंतरराष्ट्रीय मध्यस्थता केंद्र)

 

• The NDIAC was established under the New Delhi International Arbitration Centre Act, 2019, replacing the erstwhile International Centre for Alternate Dispute Resolution (ICADR), to promote India as a hub for institutional arbitration.

 

• The NDIAC was later renamed the India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC) through a 2022 amendment.

 

• Justice Hemant Gupta served as a judge of the Supreme Court of India from 2018 to 2022 and, prior to that, was Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The NDIAC headquarters is located in New Delhi and it functions as an autonomous body to conduct domestic and international arbitration, mediation and conciliation.

 

NOTE

 

• Sanjay Kishan Kaul (Option 1): A former Supreme Court judge, but he was not appointed chairperson of NDIAC.

 

• Pankaj Mithal (Option 3): A sitting Supreme Court judge, not associated with heading NDIAC.

 

• Ajay Rastogi (Option 4): A former Supreme Court judge, but not appointed as NDIAC chairperson.

question: Which of the following was the last invasion by Mahmud Ghazni outside Punjab?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Somnath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The attack on the Somnath temple in 1025 CE is regarded as Mahmud of Ghazni's last major invasion outside the Punjab region. (सोमनाथ मंदिर आक्रमण — महमूद गजनवी का अंतिम आक्रमण)

 

• Mahmud Ghazni invaded the Indian subcontinent 17 times between 1000 and 1027 CE, and the Somnath raid (1025-26 CE) was his most famous and among his last campaigns into the Indian mainland outside Punjab.

 

• The Somnath temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva and one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, situated in Gujarat, was plundered and destroyed by Mahmud during this raid.

 

• After the Somnath campaign, his only remaining expedition (1027 CE) was against the Jats of the Sindh/Indus valley, which lay within his existing territory near Punjab, not a fresh invasion into the Indian mainland outside it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahmud Ghazni's invasions mark the beginning of extensive Turkish raids into India and led to the eventual establishment of Muslim rule in parts of northern India.

 

• His court historian Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind, an important account of India during this period.

 

NOTE

 

• Mathura (Option 2): Raided by Mahmud Ghazni in 1018 CE, earlier than the Somnath campaign.

 

• Kalinjar (Option 3): Attacked around 1023 CE, before the Somnath raid.

 

• Kanauj (Option 4): Raided in 1018-19 CE, also earlier than Somnath.

question: In which year did India win its first Hockey World Cup for Men's?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1975.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won its first (and so far only) Men's Hockey World Cup in 1975, held at Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (हॉकी विश्व कप — भारत 1975)

 

• India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the final, with Ashok Kumar (son of the legendary Dhyan Chand) scoring the winning goal.

 

• The Indian team was captained by Ajit Pal Singh in the 1975 World Cup victory.

 

• The first-ever Men's Hockey World Cup was held in 1971 in Barcelona, Spain, which India did not win — India finished third in that edition (won by Pakistan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pakistan has won the Men's Hockey World Cup the most times (4 titles), followed by Netherlands and Australia.

 

• The Men's Hockey World Cup is organised by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).

 

NOTE

 

• 1971 (Option 1): The inaugural Hockey World Cup, won by Pakistan; India finished third.

 

• 1979 (Option 2): Held in Buenos Aires, won by Pakistan.

 

• 1983 (Option 4): Held in Kuala Lumpur, won by Pakistan.

question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum wavelength?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR — Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red), violet light has the shortest (minimum) wavelength, approximately 380-450 nanometres. (बैंगनी रंग — न्यूनतम तरंगदैर्ध्य)

 

• Correspondingly, violet light has the highest frequency and highest energy among visible colours, since energy is inversely proportional to wavelength (E = hc/λ).

 

• Red light, at the other end of the spectrum, has the maximum wavelength (approximately 620-750 nm) and the least energy/frequency among visible colours.

 

• When white light passes through a prism, violet bends the most (due to shortest wavelength) and red bends the least, producing the VIBGYOR spectrum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Beyond violet lies the ultraviolet region (shorter wavelength, invisible to humans); beyond red lies the infrared region (longer wavelength, invisible to humans).

 

• The phenomenon of splitting white light into its constituent colours is called dispersion, first demonstrated by Isaac Newton.

 

NOTE

 

• Yellow (Option 2): Has a longer wavelength (~570-590 nm) than violet.

 

• Green (Option 3): Has a longer wavelength (~495-570 nm) than violet.

 

• Red (Option 4): Has the maximum wavelength among VIBGYOR colours, not the minimum.

question: Which of these regions received the first wave of the Green Revolution package?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution, initiated in India in the mid-1960s under the guidance of M.S. Swaminathan, first took root in Punjab, along with parts of Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. (हरित क्रांति — पंजाब)

 

• Punjab's assured irrigation network, fertile alluvial soil, and early adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilisers and mechanised farming made it the epicentre of the first phase of the Green Revolution, primarily boosting wheat production.

 

• The success in Punjab earned it the title of the "Granary of India" / "Food Bowl of India".

 

• The Green Revolution's first phase (1966-late 1970s) was concentrated in these irrigated, resource-rich northern regions before spreading to other parts of the country in later phases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Norman Borlaug is regarded as the global "Father of the Green Revolution", while M.S. Swaminathan is called the "Father of the Green Revolution in India".

 

• Later phases of the Green Revolution extended to eastern and southern states, promoting crops like rice.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Did not receive the first wave; its terrain and cropping pattern (plantation crops) were less suited to the HYV wheat package.

 

• Western Gujarat (Option 3): Not part of the first-wave Green Revolution belt.

 

• Coastal Maharashtra (Option 4): Not part of the first-wave Green Revolution belt.

question: Which of the following initiatives of the Government of India is aimed at developing and rejuvenating 75 water bodies in each district of the country as a part of the celebration of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mission Amrit Sarovar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mission Amrit Sarovar, launched by the Government of India on 24 April 2022 (National Panchayati Raj Day), aims to develop and rejuvenate 75 water bodies (amrit sarovars) in each district of the country as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations marking 75 years of independence. (मिशन अमृत सरोवर — 75 जल निकाय)

 

• The mission targets construction/rejuvenation of at least 50,000 Amrit Sarovars across India, each covering about one acre, with a water holding capacity of about 10,000 cubic metres.

 

• It is implemented under the Ministry of Rural Development in convergence with schemes like MGNREGA.

 

• Each Amrit Sarovar site is envisaged to have plantation, a war memorial (if a martyr belongs to that gram panchayat), and facilities for the local population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav commemorates 75 years of India's independence and was officially launched on 12 March 2021.

 

• Other Amrit Mahotsav-linked initiatives include the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme and Amrit Kaal vision documents.

 

NOTE

 

• Mission Amrit Clean Water (Option 1): Not an actual government scheme name.

 

• Mission Amrit Water (Option 2): Not the correct/official name of the scheme.

 

• Mission Amrit District (Option 4): Not the correct/official name of the scheme.

question: What was the prevalence of self-reported goitre or thyroid disorder in the National Family Health Survey [NFHS-V (2019-2021)]?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.9%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), the prevalence of self-reported goitre or thyroid disorder among women aged 15-49 years in India was 2.9%. (एनएफएचएस-5 — गलगण्ड/थायरॉइड रोग 2.9%)

 

• This marked an increase from NFHS-4 (2015-16), where the self-reported prevalence of goitre/thyroid disorder was 2.2%.

 

• NFHS-5 is conducted by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, and covers a wide range of health, nutrition and demographic indicators.

 

• Thyroid disorders are more commonly self-reported among women than men, and prevalence tends to increase with age.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NFHS-5 was conducted in two phases (2019-20 and 2020-21) across all States and Union Territories of India.

 

• NFHS surveys also track other NCD indicators such as diabetes, hypertension and anaemia prevalence.

 

NOTE

 

• 3.4% (Option 2): Not the figure reported by NFHS-5 for this indicator.

 

• 4.2% (Option 3): Not the figure reported by NFHS-5 for this indicator.

 

• 2.1% (Option 4): Close to the NFHS-4 figure area but not the NFHS-5 reported value.

question: Which of these is a conventional weaker section lending under formal sector?
option_2: Self help group bank linkage model
solution_text:
The correct answer is Commercial banks priority sector lending.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priority Sector Lending (PSL) by commercial banks is the conventional, long-standing mechanism under the formal financial sector for extending credit to weaker sections of society. (प्राथमिकता प्राप्त क्षेत्र ऋण — वाणिज्यिक बैंक)

 

• Under RBI guidelines, banks are mandated to lend a specified percentage of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sectors, which explicitly includes a sub-target for weaker sections (such as SC/ST borrowers, small and marginal farmers, and persons with disabilities).

 

• This system has existed since the nationalisation of banks (1969) and is a regulated, formal-sector mechanism, unlike informal or newer alternative credit delivery models.

 

• Weaker section lending under priority sector norms is one of the oldest formal instruments of financial inclusion in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The current weaker sections sub-target under PSL is 12% of ANBC (or credit equivalent of off-balance sheet exposure, whichever is higher) for domestic commercial banks.

 

• Priority sectors also include agriculture, MSMEs, export credit, education, housing and renewable energy.

 

NOTE

 

• Money lenders (Option 1): An informal, unregulated source of rural/weaker-section credit, not a formal-sector instrument.

 

• Self help group bank linkage model (Option 2): A relatively newer, semi-formal microfinance mechanism, not the conventional formal-sector instrument.

 

• Micro finance institutions (Option 3): A newer alternative credit channel, not the conventional formal banking-sector mechanism for weaker sections.

question: The net worth of any bank is equal to ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is (reserves + loans) - liabilities.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A bank's net worth is defined as its total assets minus its total liabilities, following the basic balance-sheet identity: Net Worth = Assets - Liabilities. (बैंक की निवल संपत्ति — परिसंपत्ति घटा देयताएं)

 

• In a simplified bank balance sheet, a bank's principal assets consist of its reserves (cash held with itself/central bank) and the loans it has extended to customers.

 

• Therefore, Net worth = (Reserves + Loans) - Liabilities, where liabilities mainly comprise customer deposits.

 

• A positive net worth indicates the bank is solvent (assets exceed liabilities), while a negative net worth would indicate insolvency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• This relationship is captured in a bank's simplified T-account (balance sheet), with assets on one side and liabilities plus net worth (capital) on the other.

 

• Bank capital adequacy norms (like Basel III) require banks to maintain a minimum net worth relative to risk-weighted assets.

 

NOTE

 

• liabilities - assets (Option 1): This is the inverse relationship and would give a negative net worth figure, not the correct definition.

 

• interest + liabilities (Option 3): Interest is a flow/income item, not part of the net worth (stock) identity.

 

• (reserves + loans) + liabilities (Option 4): Incorrectly adds liabilities instead of subtracting them.

question: Who among the following personalities is a Sarod Maestro?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Amjad Ali Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is one of India's most renowned sarod maestros, belonging to the Senia Bangash gharana. (उस्ताद अमजद अली खान — सरोद वादक)

 

• He is a recipient of the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and has been conferred honours for his lifelong contribution to Hindustani classical music on the sarod.

 

• His sons, Amaan Ali Khan and Ayaan Ali Khan, have also carried forward the sarod tradition.

 

• The sarod is a stringed, fretless instrument central to Hindustani classical music, known for its deep, resonant sound.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous sarod players include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Pandit Buddhadev Dasgupta.

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan hails from Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (Option 1): A legendary shehnai player, recipient of the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain (Option 2): A world-renowned tabla maestro.

 

• Hariprasad Chaurasia (Option 3): A celebrated bansuri (flute) player.

question: Which of the following metal salts is responsible for permanent hardness in water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaCl2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Permanent hardness of water is caused by the presence of chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, such as CaCl2, MgCl2, CaSO4 and MgSO4. (स्थायी कठोरता — कैल्शियम क्लोराइड)

 

• Unlike temporary hardness, permanent hardness cannot be removed by simple boiling; it requires methods like ion-exchange, the Clark's process, or use of washing soda (sodium carbonate).

 

• CaCl2 (calcium chloride) dissolved in water dissociates to release Ca2+ ions, which combine with soap to form insoluble scum, preventing lather formation — a hallmark of hard water.

 

• In contrast, Ca(HCO3)2 (calcium bicarbonate) is responsible for temporary hardness, which is removed on boiling because it decomposes into insoluble calcium carbonate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hard water causes scaling in boilers, pipes and reduces the efficiency of soap.

 

• Hardness of water is generally expressed in terms of CaCO3 equivalents (ppm).

 

NOTE

 

• KCl (Option 1): Potassium chloride does not contribute to water hardness.

 

• NaCl (Option 2): Common salt (sodium chloride) does not cause hardness in water.

 

• Ca(HCO3)2 (Option 3): Causes temporary, not permanent, hardness, since it decomposes on boiling.

question: Who among the following personalities coined the term ‘Odissi’ for Odisha’s classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabichandra Kalicharan Patnaik.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kabichandra Kalicharan Patnaik (also spelt Kalicharan Pattnaik), an eminent Oriya poet, playwright and researcher, is credited with coining the term ‘Odissi’ for the classical dance form of Odisha, which was earlier referred to by other names such as ‘Orissi Nritya’. (कालीचरण पटनायक — ओडिसी नामकरण)

 

• Born in 1898 in Badamba, Odisha, he made significant contributions to Odia theatre, dance and music, and his compositions are still used in traditional Odissi performances.

 

• The renaming to ‘Odissi’ helped standardise and popularise the dance form's identity, aligning it with the state's name, Odisha.

 

• Odissi was later given the status of a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was one of the most influential exponents/gurus who popularised and refined Odissi technique in the 20th century, though he did not coin the name.

 

• Other pioneers in reviving Odissi include Guru Deba Prasad Das and Guru Pankaj Charan Das.

 

NOTE

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra (Option 2): A legendary Odissi guru and exponent, but not the one who coined the term.

 

• Raja Rammohan Roy (Option 3): A 19th-century social reformer, founder of Brahmo Samaj, unrelated to Odissi's nomenclature.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 4): A poet and Nobel laureate associated with Rabindra Sangeet and Santiniketan, not the naming of Odissi.

question: Deepavali is celebrated in which month of Hindu calendar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kartika.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Deepavali (Diwali) is celebrated on the Amavasya (new moon) of the Hindu month of Kartika, typically falling in October-November of the Gregorian calendar. (दीपावली — कार्तिक मास)

 

• It marks the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana and completing 14 years of exile, and is celebrated as the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil.

 

• The festival spans five days, including Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi (Choti Diwali), Diwali (Lakshmi Puja), Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.

 

• Kartika is the eighth month in the traditional Hindu lunisolar calendar (Amanta reckoning used in most of India).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other festivals also associated with the month of Kartika include Kartik Purnima and Chhath Puja (in some regions).

 

• The Hindu calendar follows a lunisolar system, with months named Chaitra, Vaishakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashwin, Kartika, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha, and Phalguna.

 

NOTE

 

• Magha (Option 1): Associated with festivals like Vasant Panchami and Maghi Purnima, not Diwali.

 

• Chaitra (Option 2): The first month of the Hindu calendar, associated with Chaitra Navratri and Hindu New Year.

 

• Ashwin (Option 3): The month of Sharad Navratri and Dussehra, which precedes Diwali but is not when Diwali itself falls.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest population density?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Bihar recorded the highest population density among Indian states, at approximately 1,102 persons per sq. km. (बिहार — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या घनत्व राज्य)

 

• Bihar's high density is attributed to its fertile Gangetic plains, predominantly agrarian economy, and high birth rates.

 

• Among Union Territories, Delhi has the highest population density in India (about 11,320 persons per sq. km as per Census 2011).

 

• West Bengal (~1,029/sq km) and Kerala (~860/sq km) also have high densities but rank below Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest population density among Indian states as per Census 2011.

 

• India's overall population density as per Census 2011 was 382 persons per sq. km.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Has India's highest total population but a lower density (~828/sq km) than Bihar.

 

• West Bengal (Option 3): Density (~1,029/sq km) is high but less than Bihar's.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Density (~860/sq km) is lower than Bihar's.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is NOT borrowed from the Canadian constitution?
option_4: Appointment of state governor by the centre
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concurrent list.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Concurrent List, a feature under which both the Union and State legislatures can make laws on the same subjects, was borrowed by the Indian Constitution from the Australian Constitution, not the Canadian Constitution. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलियाई संविधान से)

 

• From Canada, India borrowed features such as a federation with a strong centre, residuary powers vesting with the Centre, appointment of state governors by the Centre, and the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

 

• India's Constitution is often described as a "borrowed constitution" or a "bag of borrowings" since it draws features from various constitutions of the world while adapting them to Indian conditions.

 

• The scheme of the Concurrent List allows both Parliament and State legislatures to legislate on matters like education, forests, and marriage, with Union law prevailing in case of conflict (Article 254).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Australian-inspired features include the freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse and the language of the Preamble.

 

• From the UK, India borrowed parliamentary government, rule of law, and the concept of a single citizenship.

 

NOTE

 

• Advisory jurisdiction of supreme court (Option 1): Borrowed from the Canadian Constitution.

 

• Federation with strong centre (Option 2): Borrowed from the Canadian Constitution.

 

• Appointment of state governor by the centre (Option 4): Borrowed from the Canadian Constitution.

question: Which of the following is a kind of Xanthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Microbial gum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Xanthan gum is a type of microbial gum, produced through the **fermentation of sugars (like glucose or sucrose) by the bacterium *Xanthomonas campestris***. (जैंथन गोंद — सूक्ष्मजैविक गोंद)

 

• It is widely used as a thickening, stabilising and emulsifying agent in the food industry (sauces, dressings), as well as in cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and oil drilling fluids.

 

• Xanthan gum is valued for its ability to maintain viscosity across a wide range of temperatures and pH levels, and its pseudoplastic (shear-thinning) behaviour.

 

• Other examples of microbial gums include dextran and gellan gum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guar gum and locust bean gum are common examples of seed gums.

 

• Agar and carrageenan are common examples of seaweed (marine) gums.

 

NOTE

 

• Seed gum (Option 1): Examples include guar gum and locust bean gum, not xanthan.

 

• Seaweed gum (Option 2): Examples include agar and carrageenan, not xanthan.

 

• Exudate gum (Option 4): Examples include gum arabic and gum tragacanth (plant exudates), not xanthan.

question: The Muhammedan Literary Society founded in Calcutta in 1863 was founded by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nawab Abdul Latif.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mohammedan Literary Society was founded in Calcutta in 1863 by Nawab Abdul Latif, aimed at promoting modern Western education among Muslims while also preserving interest in Islamic and Persian/Urdu literature. (मुहम्मडन लिटरेरी सोसाइटी — नवाब अब्दुल लतीफ)

 

• Nawab Abdul Latif served as a government official and worked to bridge traditional Islamic education with Western learning, encouraging Muslims to take up English education without abandoning their religious and cultural identity.

 

• The society organised lectures and discussions on literary, social and religious topics, and served as an important early platform for Muslim intellectual and social reform in Bengal.

 

• This society is distinct from the Aligarh Movement led later by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh in 1875, which later became Aligarh Muslim University.

 

• Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiyya movement in 1889 at Qadian, Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (Option 2): Founder of the Ahmadiyya movement, not the Mohammedan Literary Society.

 

• Sayyid Ahmad (Option 3): Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi led the Wahhabi/Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya movement, unrelated to this society.

 

• Syed Ahmad Khan (Option 4): Founded the Aligarh Movement and MAO College, a separate and later initiative.

question: Which of the following states is the largest producer of jowar in India, as of 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maharashtra is the largest producer of jowar (sorghum) in India, accounting for the largest share of the country's jowar cultivation area and output. (ज्वार — महाराष्ट्र सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

 

• Jowar is a major kharif and rabi coarse cereal (millet) crop, extensively grown in the semi-arid regions of Maharashtra, particularly in districts like Solapur, Ahmednagar and Beed.

 

• Karnataka ranks as the second-largest producer of jowar in India, followed by other states.

 

• Jowar is drought-resistant and well-suited to the dry, less-irrigated tracts of the Deccan Plateau.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India observed 2018 as the National Year of Millets, and the UN declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets to promote crops like jowar, bajra and ragi.

 

• Jowar is a key ingredient in the traditional "bhakri" flatbread of Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): A jowar-producing state, but not the largest producer.

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): The second-largest producer of jowar in India, after Maharashtra.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): A jowar-producing state, but not the largest producer.

question: The structural part of the Indian Constitution is, to a large extent, derived from the Act of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1935.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The structural part of the Indian Constitution — including the federal scheme, judiciary, public service commissions, emergency provisions, and administrative details — is derived largely from the Government of India Act, 1935. (भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 — संरचनात्मक भाग)

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 is regarded as the single most important source of the Indian Constitution among the pre-independence legislations, providing nearly the entire administrative and structural framework.

 

• While the structural/administrative details come from the 1935 Act, the philosophical part (Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles) draws from other sources like the US and Irish Constitutions.

 

• The 1935 Act had introduced provincial autonomy and an All-India Federation (though the federal part never came into force).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

 

• The Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in provinces.

 

NOTE

 

• 1909 (Option 1): The Morley-Minto Reforms, not the main structural source of the Constitution.

 

• 1947 (Option 3): The Indian Independence Act, which granted independence, but not the source of the Constitution's structural framework.

 

• 1919 (Option 4): The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, introduced dyarchy, but not the primary structural source.

question: Which of the following is a type of vegetation found in the Himalayan region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alpine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alpine vegetation is found in the higher reaches of the Himalayan region (roughly above 3,600 m altitude), consisting of stunted trees, shrubs, grasses and mosses adapted to cold, high-altitude conditions. (अल्पाइन वनस्पति — हिमालय क्षेत्र)

 

• As altitude increases in the Himalayas, vegetation transitions through tropical, temperate, and finally to alpine forests and grasslands, before giving way to permanent snow line.

 

• Common alpine vegetation includes silver fir, junipers, pines, and alpine pastures used for grazing, along with alpine flowers like the Himalayan blue poppy.

 

• Alpine vegetation zones are found at similar altitudinal bands in mountain ranges worldwide, including the Alps (after which the vegetation type is named).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Below the alpine zone, the Himalayas host temperate forests (oak, deodar, chir pine) and further down, tropical/sub-tropical forests.

 

• The Valley of Flowers National Park in Uttarakhand is a well-known example of Himalayan alpine vegetation.

 

NOTE

 

• Mangrove (Option 1): Found in coastal, tidal areas (e.g., Sundarbans), not the Himalayan region.

 

• Pampas (Option 2): Temperate grasslands found in South America (Argentina), not in India.

 

• Savannah (Option 3): Tropical grasslands typically found in Africa and parts of peninsular India, not the Himalayan high-altitude zone.

question: Padma Bhushan Kumari Kamala is associated with which Indian dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kumari Kamala, who received the Padma Bhushan in 1970, trained in Kathak under Lachhu Maharaj in Bombay in her early years. (कुमारी कमला — पद्म भूषण 1970)

 

• She was a versatile dancer-actress who also received extensive training in Bharatanatyam (notably the Vazhuvoor style), and is chiefly remembered today as a pioneering Bharatanatyam exponent and film artiste from Tamil Nadu.

 

• Kumari Kamala performed before Queen Elizabeth II in 1953 and toured China and Japan in the late 1950s as part of Indian cultural delegations.

 

• She passed away in 2023 at the age of 91, widely eulogised as a legend of Indian classical dance and cinema.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kumari Kamala is best known to the general public for revitalising Bharatanatyam through her Tamil film dance sequences in the 1940s-50s, alongside her Kathak training.

 

• NOTE: Several independent sources describe Kumari Kamala primarily as a Bharatanatyam dancer (Vazhuvoor style), which is not among the options offered here; some question variants of this item list Bharatanatyam as an option instead of Kathak. As per the source paper's marked key (and matching the officially circulated key for this specific question), Kathak is retained as the answer.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 1): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala; not associated with Kumari Kamala.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): A classical dance form of Odisha; not associated with Kumari Kamala.

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 4): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh; not associated with Kumari Kamala.

question: SRD Prasad received the Padma Shri in 2023, for his contribution to the sport of ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalaripayattu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SRD Prasad, a veteran coach and master of Kalaripayattu, was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2023 for his contribution to this ancient martial art form. (कलरीपयट्टु — एसआरडी प्रसाद, पद्म श्री 2023)

 

• Kalaripayattu is one of the world's oldest martial art forms, originating in Kerala, combining strikes, kicks, grappling and weapon-based techniques.

 

• The 2023 Padma Shri sports category also honoured coaches like K. Sanathoiba Sharma (for Thang-Ta) and Gurcharan Singh (cricket coaching).

 

• Kalaripayattu training traditionally takes place in a specially constructed pit called a "kalari".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are India's highest civilian honours after the Bharat Ratna, given in the categories of Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

 

• Kalaripayattu is believed to have influenced other Asian martial arts traditions due to historical trade and cultural links.

• Jallikattu (Option 1): A bull-taming sport traditionally practised in Tamil Nadu, not linked to SRD Prasad's award.

 

• Boat Racing (Option 3): Associated with traditional snake-boat races (Vallam Kali) in Kerala, not the reason for this award.

 

• Seval Sandai (Option 4): Refers to traditional cockfighting in Tamil Nadu, not the reason for this award.

question: While computing Net Economic Welfare (NEW), which of the following items is subtracted from GNP?
option_2: Adjustments for congestion of urban life
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adjustments for congestion of urban life.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net Economic Welfare (NEW), a concept proposed by economists William Nordhaus and James Tobin, adjusts GNP to better reflect economic well-being by adding beneficial non-market activities and subtracting negative externalities. (शुद्ध आर्थिक कल्याण — नगरीय भीड़भाड़ हेतु समायोजन घटाया जाता है)

 

• Negative factors like pollution, environmental degradation, and congestion/disamenities of urban life are subtracted from GNP while computing NEW, since they reduce actual welfare despite not being deducted in standard GNP accounting.

 

• In contrast, beneficial non-market contributions such as the value of leisure time and do-it-yourself (household) activities are added to GNP, as they enhance welfare but are excluded from conventional GNP.

 

• NEW was introduced to address the limitation that GNP does not account for the quality of life, environmental costs, and non-market welfare contributions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of NEW is closely related to Measure of Economic Welfare (MEW), an earlier formulation by Nordhaus and Tobin (1972).

 

• Other welfare-adjusted measures include the Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI) and Green GDP.

 

NOTE

 

• Value of leisure time (Option 1): This is added to GNP while computing NEW, not subtracted.

 

• Do-it-yourself activities (Option 3): This is added to GNP while computing NEW, not subtracted.

 

• The underground economy (Option 4): Adjustments for the underground/informal economy are typically added (since it represents unrecorded but real production), not subtracted.

question: In India, ________________ fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) — the minimum percentage of a bank's total deposits that it must maintain as cash reserves with the central bank — is fixed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). (नकद आरक्षित अनुपात — भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक)

 

• CRR is one of the key monetary policy tools used by the RBI, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, to regulate money supply and control inflation/liquidity in the economy.

 

• The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and the RBI's Central Board periodically review and revise the CRR as part of monetary policy actions.

 

• A higher CRR reduces the funds available with banks for lending, thereby tightening liquidity, while a lower CRR increases lendable funds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key monetary policy instruments controlled by RBI include the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), Repo Rate, and Reverse Repo Rate.

 

• The RBI was established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949; it functions as India's central bank.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): Handles fiscal policy and the Union Budget, not the CRR, which is a monetary policy tool controlled by RBI.

 

• Ministry of External Affairs (Option 3): Deals with India's foreign relations, unrelated to monetary policy.

 

• State Bank of India (Option 4): A public sector commercial bank; it does not fix the CRR, but is itself subject to it.
